36673028.model_family: few-shot learning similarity-measure network (compared to SVM, random forest)
36673028.clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder diagnosis from resting-state fMRI
36673028.patient_population: individuals with ASD from the multi-site ABIDE database (age not specified in abstract; framed as pediatric ASD diagnosis)
36673028.model_description: A few-shot learning approach measures similarity between resting-state fMRI connectivity patterns from different sites, training a similarity function to improve generalization across the heterogeneous multi-site ABIDE dataset. It classifies scans as autism spectrum disorder or not, and was compared against SVM and random forest baselines on accuracy, precision and F1 score.
36673028.dataset_size: ABIDE multi-site database (site-level results reported, e.g. TRINITY site)
36673028.headline_result: Accuracy on the TRINITY site over 5% higher than comparison methods (SVM, random forest)

36796856.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — seed-based functional connectivity statistical analysis only

36813977.model_family: point estimation, ranking learning and scoring modules (deep learning-based ordinal regression)
36813977.body_region: hand and wrist (radius, ulna, phalanges, metacarpals)
36813977.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity / bone age assessment (TW3-RUS method)
36813977.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (male and female cohorts)
36813977.model_description: The system, called PEARLS, takes hand radiographs and automatically localizes key bones (radius, ulna, phalanges, metacarpals) used in the TW3-RUS method, scores each bone's maturity stage with an ordinal ranking model, and outputs a bone age via two standard transform curves. It replaces manual staging to reduce rater variability.
36813977.headline_result: Mean average precision of bone point localization 86.29%; stage determination precision 97.33%; bone age assessment accuracy 96.8% within 1 year

36869224.exclusion_reason: adult-only cohort (mean age 23.2); AI predictive analytics applied to non-imaging maltreatment history data, not to imaging

36881467.exclusion_reason: non-imaging NLP on patient-generated free text, not a radiology application

36994163.model_family: hierarchical (shifted-window) vision transformer for cortical surface meshes
36994163.clinical_problem: neonatal brain phenotyping and cortical parcellation from surface MRI data
36994163.patient_population: neonates (preterm and term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP); also tested on adult UK Biobank and MindBoggle datasets
36994163.model_description: A transformer backbone processes cortical surface meshes by applying self-attention within local mesh windows and merging patches hierarchically, producing representations usable for multiple downstream tasks. It was evaluated for predicting neonatal phenotypes from dHCP surface data and, built into a segmentation architecture, for cortical parcellation on adult datasets.
36994163.release_evidence: Code and trained models are publicly available at https://github.com/metrics-lab/surface-vision-transformers
36994163.dataset_size: dHCP neonatal dataset; UK Biobank and MindBoggle datasets for parcellation
36994163.headline_result: Outperforms existing surface deep learning methods for neonatal phenotyping prediction; competitive results on cortical parcellation on UK Biobank and MindBoggle

37008220.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — anatomically weighted functional connectivity is a statistical model, not a learned classifier

37008947.model_family: real-time object detection models + Key Bone Search post-processing + LightGBM regression, converted to ONNX
37008947.body_region: hand and wrist (13 key bones, RUS-CHN method)
37008947.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment
37008947.model_description: Hand radiographs are processed with real-time object-detection models to locate and grade 13 key bones per the RUS-CHN method, then a LightGBM regression model converts those grades into a bone age. The pipeline was optimized (ONNX) to run in real time on GPU, outputting bone age alongside the location and developmental grade of each key bone to assist the physician.
37008947.headline_result: Mean absolute error 0.35 years, RMSE 0.46 years, RMSPE 0.11; inference 26 ms for bone grading/location and 2 ms for bone age on GPU

37086604.exclusion_reason: adult-only cohort (ages 18-23); no trained AI/ML model, seed-based connectivity comparison only

37182338.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — graph-theoretic network efficiency and mediation analysis

37240663.model_family: feature selection (two-sample t-test, LASSO) with predictive modeling of resting-state fMRI features
37240663.clinical_problem: predicting response to electroconvulsive therapy in adolescents with treatment-refractory depression
37240663.patient_population: 40 adolescents with treatment-refractory depression treated with ECT
37240663.model_description: Resting-state fMRI measures (ALFF, fALFF, ReHo, and functional connectivity) were extracted before treatment, screened with a two-sample t-test and LASSO, and used to build a model predicting clinical response to electroconvulsive therapy. The best-performing features involved the insula, parietal and frontal gyri, and cortico-limbic connections.
37240663.headline_result: Best predictive model achieved AUC > 0.8 for predicting ECT treatment response

37310327.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — group-comparison regression analysis of resting-state connectivity

37528599.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — correlation/statistical analysis of DTI metrics

37531941.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — graph-theoretic statistical network analysis

37639906.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — independent component analysis used to characterize networks, not for diagnosis or prediction

37690162.exclusion_reason: adult-only cohort (bereaved parents); not a pediatric imaging study

37735232.clinical_problem: adult height prediction from bone age assessment
37735232.model_description: BoneXpert automatically reads bone age from hand radiographs and its output is fed into adult-height-prediction models, compared against manual bone age readings by two expert radiologists. The study compares BoneXpert-based and manual-reading-based adult height predictions against measured population height.
37735232.release_evidence: BoneXpert is referenced with a registered trademark (BoneXpert®) as an existing automated commercial bone age reading method
37735232.headline_result: BoneXpert-based adult height prediction had the smallest difference from population mean height for males; manual readings showed up to 43% of interobserver predictions differing by more than 5 cm

37807577.clinical_problem: predicting autism spectrum disorder risk in offspring from parental sensory profile
37807577.patient_population: 30 children with ASD, 26 matched controls, and their 48 biological parents
37807577.model_description: Sensory fMRI responses to sensory stimuli were measured in children with and without ASD and in their biological parents. A machine learning model trained on the parents' sensory response profile was used to predict the likelihood of autism spectrum disorder in their offspring.
37807577.headline_result: Parental sensory profile predicted offspring ASD likelihood with 71.4% accuracy

37898019.model_family: graph convolutional neural network (deep learning) with a custom loss function
37898019.clinical_problem: predicting functional brain connectivity from structural connectivity in early childhood
37898019.patient_population: children longitudinally scanned at 1, 2, 4, and 6 years of age (N=360), compared with adults (N=89)
37898019.model_description: A graph convolutional neural network with a novel loss function is trained to predict an individual's functional brain connectivity from their structural (white matter) connectivity, using longitudinal MRI from children scanned at ages 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a comparison adult sample. It improved on existing models at predicting functional connectivity from structural data.
37898019.headline_result: Deep learning model improved prediction of individual functional connectivity from structural connectivity compared to existing models

37939442.clinical_problem: predicting treatment response in major depressive episode
37939442.patient_population: 198 adolescents and young adults with major depressive episode
37939442.model_description: Baseline resting-state functional connectivity from fMRI is fed into a Graph Isomorphism Network, a deep learning model, to predict whether an individual adolescent or young adult with a major depressive episode will respond to treatment. The most discriminating regions were in paralimbic and subcortical brain areas.
37939442.headline_result: Predicted 79.8% of responders and 67.4% of non-responders (overall accuracy 74.24%)

37946742.clinical_problem: imputing missing structural brain MRI measurements across datasets
37946742.patient_population: adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (N=3760, minimum age 12) and the NCANDA adolescent cohort (N=540)
37946742.model_description: A graph neural network models dependencies between structural MRI regions-of-interest measurements and predicts values missing from one public dataset (ABCD) using a model trained on a related dataset (NCANDA) that shares some of the same measurements. It also accounts for demographic differences such as sex, and the imputed measurements improved downstream sex-classification accuracy.
37946742.headline_result: 5-fold cross-validation on NCANDA showed imputed scores more accurate than linear regression and other deep learning models; improved sex-classification accuracy when added as features

38183676.exclusion_reason: broad review of AI across pediatric endocrinology (diabetes, obesity, facial recognition, omics); not focused on radiology imaging AI

38184159.exclusion_reason: no diagnostic AI/ML model — dynamic causal modeling of effective connectivity, a hypothesis-driven statistical method

38185571.clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder from white matter microstructure
38185571.patient_population: 62 children with autism spectrum disorder and 44 typically developing children
38185571.model_description: Multi-shell diffusion MRI is processed to compute diffusion tensor, diffusion kurtosis, and white matter tract integrity metrics along white matter tracts. The metrics that differed significantly between groups were used to train an XGBoost model to classify children as having autism spectrum disorder or being typically developing, with SHAP values used to rank feature importance.
38185571.dataset_size: 62 children with ASD, 44 typically developing controls
38185571.headline_result: XGBoost model demonstrated excellent classification ability distinguishing ASD from typically developing children (exact AUC not given)

38217837.exclusion_reason: unsupervised hierarchical clustering for a wellbeing research question, not a diagnostic/predictive radiology AI application

38282240.exclusion_reason: NLP applied to free-text injury records, not to CT images; descriptive epidemiology study with no imaging AI model

38321313.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the growth plate on diffusion tensor imaging to predict height change
38321313.model_description: A UNETR deep-learning model automatically segments the physis and metaphysis on diffusion tensor MRI of the femur, replacing time-consuming manual segmentation used to derive diffusion biomarkers of growth. It was trained and validated on 385 DTI scans from 191 subjects and compared against a standard UNET and manual segmentation.
38321313.headline_result: Mean Dice 0.81 for UNETR vs 0.68 for UNET; segmentation took <1 s per volume (vs 15 min manual); ICC for femur diffusion metrics 0.87-0.97
38321313.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation

38326559.model_family: automatic machine learning pipeline (feature engineering, selection, and model optimization)
38326559.clinical_problem: classifying obsessive-compulsive disorder from diffusion white matter measures
38326559.patient_population: 1,336 adults (690 OCD, 646 controls) and 317 pediatric participants (175 OCD, 142 controls) from 18 international sites
38326559.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging white matter estimates from 18 international sites were combined into the largest OCD DTI dataset to date. An automated machine learning pipeline was trained to classify OCD versus healthy controls, and unmedicated versus medicated OCD, separately in adult and pediatric cohorts, with leave-one-site-out cross-validation to test generalizability across sites.
38326559.headline_result: OCD vs healthy control classification AUC 59.8 ± 7.39 in children (57.19 ± 3.47 in adults); low-to-moderate accuracy overall, with significant site variability (children AUC range 35.9-63.2)

38354445.model_family: eight common machine learning models (best: logistic regression) on automated fiber quantification features
38354445.clinical_problem: identifying pediatric myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) from white matter microstructure
38354445.patient_population: 28 children with MOGAD and 31 healthy controls
38354445.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging is processed with automated fiber quantification to measure microstructure along 100 nodes per white matter tract. Metrics that differed significantly between children with MOGAD and healthy controls were used to train and compare eight machine learning classifiers to identify MOGAD, with the tract metrics also correlated to clinical disability scores.
38354445.headline_result: All machine learning models achieved AUC > 0.85 for identifying MOGAD; best performance with logistic regression, AUC 0.952

38370839.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — whole-brain voxel-wise regression analysis

38455757.clinical_problem: early identification of refractory constipation in children
38455757.patient_population: children with functional constipation (n=77), refractory constipation (n=63), or no constipation (n=65)
38455757.model_description: Standardized colon size ratios measured on barium enema (sigmoid, descending, transverse, rectum, rectosigmoid) were used to train a linear support vector machine that classifies children into functional constipation, refractory constipation, or non-constipation groups, aiming to flag refractory disease earlier.
38455757.headline_result: 81% accuracy (95% CI 79.17-83.19%) distinguishing refractory constipation from the other groups

38640643.exclusion_reason: adult-only cohort (mean age 24); no trained AI/ML model, standard psychophysiological-interaction fMRI analysis

38645622.exclusion_reason: adult fMRI language benchmark; not a pediatric patient population (the AI training-data size is developmentally motivated, but study subjects are adults)

38650167.exclusion_reason: ML predicts imaging-derived metrics from non-imaging behavioral/sleep data; not an imaging-based diagnostic AI tool

38659616.clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder recognition from functional connectivity
38659616.patient_population: children younger than 12 years old from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE)
38659616.model_description: Regions of interest from resting-state fMRI are treated as nodes of a graph, with wavelet-decomposed BOLD signal features and a functional-connectivity-derived adjacency matrix. A graph attention network with self-attention and node-selection pooling layers classifies scans for autism spectrum disorder while also highlighting the brain regions driving the prediction, improving interpretability over prior deep learning approaches.
38659616.headline_result: Superior performance compared to recent similar ASD-classification studies (exact accuracy not given in abstract)

38668397.model_family: commercially available vendor deep learning denoising reconstruction algorithm
38668397.body_region: knee growth plate (femoral and tibial physis)
38668397.clinical_problem: image quality of diffusion tensor imaging of the pediatric growth plate
38668397.patient_population: children undergoing knee DTI at a tertiary pediatric center
38668397.model_description: A vendor-provided deep learning denoising reconstruction algorithm (75% noise reduction) was applied to knee DTI scans acquired at two spatial resolutions in children, and diffusion tract metrics (count, volume, length, fractional anisotropy) were compared between denoised and non-denoised scans to assess whether denoising preserves or alters quantitative growth-plate diffusion measurements.
38668397.release_evidence: the MR vendor-provided a commercially available DL model
38668397.dataset_size: prospective study; exact N not stated in abstract
38668397.headline_result: Deep learning reconstruction significantly changed several diffusion metrics (e.g., decreased femorotibial FA, p<0.01) versus non-denoised scans at smaller voxel size

38712238.clinical_problem: estimating brain maturity (brain age) from the neonatal connectome
38712238.patient_population: 611 infants in the first month of life (174 preterm, 437 term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project
38712238.model_description: Resting-state fMRI and diffusion MRI connectomes from newborns are used to train connectome-based predictive models that estimate postmenstrual age. The gap between predicted and actual age (the 'brain age gap') is used as a marker of deviation from normal brain development, and was linked to perinatal exposures and later toddler behavior.
38712238.headline_result: Structural and functional connectomes accurately predicted postmenstrual age in both term and preterm infants; brain age gap associated with perinatal exposures and toddler outcomes

38714204.exclusion_reason: non-imaging AI: NLP used only for cohort identification from EHR; outcome prediction uses standard logistic regression on clinical/lab variables, not an imaging AI model

38774602.model_family: heterogeneous graph convolutional neural network via Hodge-Laplacian spectral filters
38774602.clinical_problem: predicting general intelligence from brain functional connectivity
38774602.patient_population: children from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (n=7,693)
38774602.model_description: A new graph neural network architecture applies Hodge-Laplacian-based spectral filters to model brain fMRI data at both regional (node) and connection (edge) levels, with a topological pooling method. Trained on ABCD fMRI data, it predicts children's general intelligence from functional connectivity and outperforms several existing graph neural network architectures.
38774602.headline_result: HL-HGCNN outperformed state-of-the-art graph neural networks (GAT, BrainGNN, dGCN, BrainNetCNN, Hypergraph NN) in predicting general intelligence from fMRI

38857141.clinical_problem: estimating perinatal brain age / maturity from cortical morphology
38857141.patient_population: 531 preterm and full-term neonates from the Developing Human Connectome Project; validated on an additional cohort from the Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child-care Hospital, plus 47 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age
38857141.model_description: A graph-attention-based network estimates an infant's brain age from cortical folding metrics (mean curvature, sulcal depth), explicitly modeling the relationship between brain hemispheres to capture structural lateralization during early development. It was tested on dHCP neonates and an independent external hospital cohort, and applied to preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age to detect developmental delay.
38857141.dataset_size: 531 neonates (dHCP); external validation cohort (Gansu); 47 preterm infants at term-equivalent age
38857141.headline_result: Mean absolute error 0.53, R² 0.89 for perinatal brain age; predicted age significantly lower than chronological age in preterm infants at term-equivalent age, indicating delayed brain maturation
38857141.study_design: retrospective multi-center technical development and validation

38906229.exclusion_reason: systematic review with no AI/ML component — conventional structural MRI/EEG correlates of Theory-of-Mind deficits

39010829.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — graph-theoretic brain efficiency and generalized estimating equations

39046114.clinical_problem: estimating brain age and its relationship to mathematical performance
39046114.patient_population: youth and adults aged 7-30 undergoing task-based fMRI during nonsymbolic magnitude processing
39046114.model_description: Task-based fMRI connectivity features from the frontoparietal and salience networks during a magnitude-processing task are fed into a Gradient Boosting model to predict chronological (brain) age across ages 7-30. A more mature predicted brain age was associated with better arithmetic performance.
39046114.dataset_size: ages 7-30, independent training and test datasets (N not given)
39046114.headline_result: Brain age prediction correlation r=.727, mean absolute error 2.944 years

39153232.model_family: neural network algorithm combining demographics, DTI, and graph-theory network metrics
39153232.clinical_problem: diagnosing first-episode major depressive disorder in pubertal children/adolescents from white matter and network changes
39153232.patient_population: 36 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder (mean age 15.8) and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age 15.2)
39153232.model_description: Whole-brain diffusion tensor imaging and graph-theory network topology metrics are combined with demographic data and fed into a neural network model to distinguish first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls, identifying white matter and network hub abnormalities linked to symptom severity.
39153232.headline_result: Diagnostic model achieved AUROC 0.88 and F1 score 0.80

39182062.exclusion_reason: non-imaging study — gut microbiota sequencing, not diagnostic imaging

39182418.model_family: machine learning models on movie-watching fMRI connectivity
39182418.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive abilities (IQ and related measures) in children and adolescents with ADHD from functional connectivity
39182418.patient_population: children and adolescents aged 6-16 (373 with ADHD, 106 neurotypical) undergoing movie-watching fMRI
39182418.model_description: Functional connectivity patterns recorded while children and adolescents watched a short movie during fMRI were used to train machine learning models that predict IQ and other cognitive measures (visual-spatial, verbal comprehension, fluid reasoning), evaluated with out-of-sample cross-validation. The models successfully predicted these measures in younger children (6-11) with ADHD but not in adolescents (12-16) with ADHD.
39182418.dataset_size: 373 children/adolescents with ADHD, 106 neurotypical controls, ages 6-16
39182418.headline_result: Machine learning models predicted IQ and cognitive measures in early/middle childhood (ages 6-11) with ADHD but failed to generalize to adolescents (12-16)

39221654.model_family: AI-based automated bone age assessment software
39221654.model_description: Two commercially available AI bone age assessment programs, BoneXpert and VUNO Med-Bone Age, were compared against manual Greulich-Pyle bone age readings by two radiologists in a Turkish pediatric cohort, to assess agreement between the AI tools and manual assessment.
39221654.release_evidence: BoneXpert and VUNO Med-Bone Age are named commercially available AI-based bone age assessment programs
39221654.headline_result: ICC for AI vs manual agreement: VUNO 0.995 (boys)/0.994 (girls), BoneXpert 0.994 (boys)/0.995 (girls); no significant difference between the two AI tools
39221654.study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy / agreement study

39238165.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — functional connectivity multivariate pattern analysis used descriptively, not for diagnosis or prediction

39251706.exclusion_reason: predicts socioeconomic status from brain connectome; not a clinical/radiology diagnostic application

39287215.exclusion_reason: clinical prognostic model built on structured/tabular variables (including radiographic measurements), not an imaging-analysis AI tool

39320999.model_family: explainable deep learning framework for spatio-temporal coupling (dynamic functional connectivity)
39320999.patient_population: children and young adults undergoing resting-state functional imaging
39320999.model_description: A deep learning framework jointly models the time-varying coupling between brain regions and their connectivity (dynamic functional connectivity) while providing step-by-step explainability of the results. Applied to resting-state imaging spanning brain development, it captured two distinct patterns of change with age: decreasing connectivity in emotion-regulation regions and increasing connectivity in cognitive regions, with children and young adults showing cyclic fluctuations.
39320999.headline_result: Identified two distinct developmental functional-connectivity patterns (decreasing emotion-regulation connectivity, increasing cognitive-network connectivity) with age

39367488.exclusion_reason: study protocol paper; deep learning described only for coding behavioral video, not diagnostic radiology imaging

39368283.exclusion_reason: no trained AI/ML model — literature-based network definition and standard functional-connectivity group comparison

39442439.model_family: ensemble machine learning (balanced random forest, XGBoost, EasyEnsemble classifier)
39442439.clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of ADHD from functional connectivity biomarkers
39442439.patient_population: children with ADHD and neurotypical controls from the ADHD-200 resting-state fMRI dataset
39442439.model_description: Resting-state fMRI connectivity of auditory-visual integration brain regions was summarized with graph-theoretical features and network-based statistics, then used to train ensemble machine learning classifiers (balanced random forest, XGBoost, EasyEnsemble) to distinguish children with ADHD from neurotypical controls, addressing class imbalance in the dataset.
39442439.dataset_size: ADHD-200 dataset (exact N not given in abstract)
39442439.headline_result: Automated ADHD classification with moderate accuracy (74.30%) using an EasyEnsemble classifier on auditory-visual integration network features

39460772.patient_population: children (bone age assessment context; also discusses medicolegal age estimation)
39460772.model_description: A narrative review describing AI-based algorithms developed for radiologic bone age estimation (object recognition, feature extraction, segmentation) and their reported performance, followed by a Strengths-Weaknesses-Opportunities-Challenges (SWOC) analysis of factors affecting clinical and medicolegal adoption of AI for bone age assessment.
